query: What are the common advantage attributes of airlines whose overall rating is high?

per_column.name: cabin_crew_attitude
per_column.rationale: Crew attitude is a core 'advantage attribute' axis for high-rated airlines, giving real grouping leverage. Well grounded where crew is described (rows 1,3,4,5: 'welcoming/kind/helpful', 'well-trained on hospitality', 'came round regularly', 'friendly, cared for passengers' -> warm_proactive). But row 2 (a seat/entertainment complaint that never mentions crew) is labelled 'cold_indifferent', an unwarranted inference from overall negativity.

per_column.name: ground_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Distinct axis from onboard crew, genuinely useful. Rows 2-5 correctly return Unknown when ground service is not discussed. However row 1, an entirely onboard review, is confidently labelled 'efficient_helpful' though ground handling is never mentioned — a specific asserted where the text is silent.

per_column.name: service_proactivity
per_column.rationale: A bare boolean that largely restates the 'proactive' pole of cab_crew_attitude (warm_proactive), so it adds little independent leverage for this query. Values track the crew descriptions reasonably; 'false' for silent/negative rows is a defensible default rather than an invented fact.

per_column.name: service_consistency
per_column.rationale: Consistency (consistent_high vs inconsistent) is a meaningful comparative axis and is well populated (few NULLs). Row 5 explicitly says 'service was consistently good' -> consistent_high. Other labels are plausible readings, though consistency is somewhat inferred from single-flight sentiment (rows 1,2), a mild stretch but not contradictory.

per_column.name: food_quality
per_column.rationale: Useful but partly redundant with the original 'Food & Beverages' rating. Grounded where food is described (rows 1,3,4 'delicious/plentiful/2 full meals' -> excellent) and correctly Unknown in row 5. Row 2 mentions no food at all yet is labelled 'poor', sentiment leakage from a seat complaint.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_assessment
per_column.rationale: Overlaps with the original 'Seat Comfort' rating, reducing novelty, but the categorical detail (comfortable_spacious/cramped/broken) can still support attribute analysis. Values are sound: row1 'legroom spacious', row2 'far too narrow, poor padding' -> cramped, row5 'comfortable and wide'. Row 3's 'adequate' for a seat-silent review is a mild neutral default, acceptable.

per_column.name: baggage_handling_outcome
per_column.rationale: Plausible attribute axis but heavily dominated by 'no_issue' (5663), so it is near-constant and low-leverage for distinguishing high-rated airlines. Groundedness concern: none of the sampled reviews mention baggage, yet all are asserted 'no_issue' rather than unknown — a confident specific from silence, not merely a not-stated label.

per_column.name: customer_service_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Relevant mainly to complaint handling rather than the 'advantage' framing, giving modest leverage here. 'not_contacted' as the default for reviews that never describe contacting support (all five samples) is a reasonable not-applicable reading rather than an invented fact.

per_column.name: refund_rebooking_handling
per_column.rationale: Overwhelmingly 'not_applicable' (6206) and tangential to identifying advantages of highly-rated airlines, so it offers little analytical leverage. However the 'not_applicable' default for reviews with no refund context is correct behaviour, so groundedness is fine.

per_column.name: value_for_money_perception
per_column.rationale: Restates the original 'Value For Money' rating in categorical form, limiting new leverage. None of the sampled texts explicitly discuss price/value, yet each gets a confident label (excellent_value / poor_value_overpriced) inferred from overall sentiment; directionally reasonable but the specific 'overpriced' claim is not grounded in the text.

judge.rationale: As a set the columns open several genuine attribute axes (crew attitude, ground service, service consistency, food, seat, value, baggage, support, refunds) that let an analyst group high-rated airlines by advantage characteristics, which is exactly what the query needs. Weaknesses: a few columns (food_quality, seat_comfort_assessment, value_for_money_perception, service_proactivity) largely duplicate existing rating columns or another added column, and refund/baggage/customer-service columns are near-constant, so their marginal leverage is limited. Groundedness is decent when the attribute is explicitly described and correct 'Unknown' is used in several silent rows, but there is a systematic tendency to propagate overall review sentiment into attributes the text is silent on (row 2 'cold_indifferent'/'poor' food, row 1 'efficient_helpful' ground service, blanket 'no_issue' baggage, inferred 'overpriced' value). These are real but bounded groundedness lapses, so scores are moderate rather than low.
